definition: Running an AI system's actions (such as code execution) in an isolated environment to contain potential harm or unintended side effects.
details: Sandboxing is a critical safety measure for agentic systems that can execute code or take real-world actions, limiting the blast radius of mistakes, bugs, or malicious inputs.

explainer.lead: Sandboxing runs an AI system's actions, such as code execution, in an isolated environment. It is a critical safety measure for agentic systems that can execute code or take real-world actions, limiting the blast radius of mistakes, bugs, or malicious inputs.

tiers.eli5: Like letting someone practice driving in a walled-off lot instead of on the open road.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers isolate code execution and tool calls so failures stay contained. The pitfall is assuming isolation is complete when the sandbox has escape routes to real systems.
tiers.paperLevel: Actions are executed within an isolated environment that contains potential harm or unintended side effects. Limit: protection depends on the isolation boundary holding against mistakes and malicious inputs.

explainer.example: An agent writing and running Python has its code executed in a container with no access to production data.
